title: On the monotonization of polyhedra
contribution: A generalized monotonization of polyhedra with a sufficient condition for its facets to be facets of the original polytope, made trivially checkable for the STSP, ATSP and linear ordering polytopes (abstract).
problem_entry: Equations in the defining system make facet analysis of a less than full-dimensional polytope hard, so it is studied through its submissive or dominant; when their facets are facets of P had been posed in the literature as an important research problem (abstract).
key_idea: A generalized monotonization g-mon(P) subsuming submissive and dominant, with a sufficient condition for a facet of g-mon(P) to define a facet of P; conditions 'trivially easy to verify' for STSP, ATSP and linear ordering polytopes (abstract).
assumptions: Polytopes whose linear system has implicit or explicit equations; applied to the symmetric and asymmetric traveling salesman polytopes and the linear ordering polytope; no data model (abstract).
proof_devices: generalized monotonization g-mon(P), subsuming submissive and dominant, with a sufficient facet-transfer condition (abstract)
polytope-specific sufficient conditions, trivially easy to verify, for STSP, ATSP and linear ordering polytopes (abstract)
positioning: Answers in part a research problem posed in the literature: sufficient conditions for a facet of the submissive or dominant to be a facet of the polytope (abstract).
writing: Moves from the general difficulty to the customary workaround, then the posed problem, then a measured claim ('goes a long way towards solving this problem') (abstract).
limits_future: Sufficient, not necessary, conditions; the posed problem is not claimed fully solved (abstract).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Prove in the full-dimensional relaxation, then transfer back (existing)
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Facets are proved on a full-dimensional generalized monotonization and carried back to P by a sufficient condition, stated in general form; the S102 survey card has the same device.

transferable: When the polytope of interest has equations, prove facets on a full-dimensional monotonization and give a sufficient condition, easy to check, that carries each facet back to the original polytope (abstract).

quotes.text: It is therefore customary to approach the study of such a polytope P through the study of one of its (full dimensional) relaxations (monotonizations) known as the submissive and the dominant of P.
Our paper goes a long way towards solving this problem.

New heuristic procedures to compute near-optimal feasible solutions are proposed, which proved to be very effective to reduce the overall computing time spent by the branch-and-cut algorithm.

In the present paper the branch-and-cut algorithms by Fischetti and Toth [17] and by Applegate, Bixby, Chvátal and Cook [2] are considered and tested on a set of 35 real-world instances including 16 new instances recently presented in [12].

title: Combinatorial Benders’ cuts
contribution: Combinatorial Benders' cuts: an automatic reformulation of big-M MIPs into an integer master and an LP slave returning minimal-infeasible-subsystem cuts, solved some orders of magnitude faster on two hard classes (abstract).
problem_entry: MIPs whose logical implications are modelled with big-M coefficients are 'notoriously among the hardest to solve' (abstract).
key_idea: Remove the big-M dependence automatically: a master ILP without continuous variables, a slave LP that validates master solutions or returns combinatorial inequalities from minimal (irreducible) infeasible subsystems, separable efficiently at integer master solutions; a possibly much tighter master LP relaxation (abstract).
assumptions: MIPs with logical implications modelled by big-M coefficients; master with integer variables only, slave LP over the continuous part (abstract).
proof_devices: master ILP with no continuous variables plus a slave LP that validates master solutions (abstract)
combinatorial inequalities associated with minimal (irreducible) infeasible subsystems, separated efficiently when the master solution is integer (abstract)
experiments: Two specific classes of hard-to-solve MIPs; the reformulation solved some orders of magnitude faster than the original model; solver, machine and instances not in the abstract (abstract).
limits_future: Efficient separation is claimed only for integer master solutions (abstract).

method_links.note: Step 3: the continuous variables, and with them the big-M coefficients, are projected out into a slave LP; the master is a pure ILP (IPCO 2004 version of the S006 card's evidence).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The combinatorial inequalities 'can be separated efficiently in case the master solution is integer'.

transferable: Project out continuous variables that only carry big-M logic: keep an integer-only master and let an LP slave return cuts read from minimal infeasible subsystems (abstract).

quotes.text: Our solution scheme defines a master Integer Linear Problem (ILP) with no continuous variables, which contains combinatorial information on the integer-variable feasible combinations that can be “distilled” from the original MIP model.
The inequalities are associated to minimal (or irreducible) infeasible subsystems of a certain linear system, and can be separated efficiently in case the master solution is integer.

The computed bound is compared with that obtained when only Gomory mixed-integer cuts are used, on a large test-bed of MIPLIB instances.

title: Can Pure Cutting Plane Algorithms Work?
contribution: Shows that the lexicographic version of Gomory's fractional cutting-plane method and two mimicking heuristics radically improve on the standard method, solving stein15, stein27 and bm23 exactly (abstract).
problem_entry: The standard Gomory fractional cutting plane method closes only a tiny fraction of the integrality gap on MIPLIB instances such as stein15, stein27 and bm23 (abstract).
key_idea: Implement the lexicographic version of Gomory's fractional cutting plane method and two heuristics mimicking it, compared with the standard algorithm in single-cut and multi-cut versions (abstract).
assumptions: Pure ILPs from MIPLIB (stein15, stein27, bm23 named); Gomory fractional cuts (abstract).
proof_devices: lexicographic version of Gomory's fractional cutting plane method (abstract)
two heuristics mimicking the lexicographic method (abstract)
single-cut and multi-cut (rounds of cuts) versions of every variant (abstract)
experiments: A battery of MIPLIB problems; the standard Gomory algorithm as baseline, single-cut and multi-cut; exact solution of stein15, stein27 and bm23 (abstract).
writing: Title as a question; strong wording ('a radical improvement', 'this surprizing phenomenon') with an explanation promised (abstract).

method_links.note: Steps 3 and 6: the stalling blamed on Gomory's method is cured by changing which LP solution the loop separates (lexicographic version), with the same cut family; IPCO 2008 version of the S074 card's evidence.

transferable: When a pure cutting-plane loop stalls, keep the cut family and change which LP optimum is separated (lexicographic re-optimization), testing single-cut and multi-cut versions of every variant (abstract).

quotes.text: In particular, we report the exact solution of ILP instances from MIPLIB such as stein15, stein27, and bm23, for which the standard Gomory cutting plane algorithm is not able to close more than a tiny fraction of the integrality gap.
We also offer an explanation for this surprizing phenomenon.

title: A Relax-and-Cut Framework for Gomory's Mixed-Integer Cuts
contribution: A relax-and-cut framework that reads rank-1 GMICs from bases of the original LP and relaxes them in Lagrangian fashion instead of adding them, giving fast and accurate variants (abstract).

rank-1 GMICs read from bases of the original LP before any cut (abstract)

positioning: Against recent techniques for better GMIC quality by Balas and Bonami and by Dash and Goycoolea (abstract).

method_links.note: The instability is blamed on the round-by-round loop and the remedy changes what the unchanged GMIC generator is fed (bases of the original LP, Lagrangian relaxation of the cuts); CPAIOR 2010 version of the S095 card's evidence.

quotes.text: Unfortunately, this approach prone to instability.
We adopt a relax-and-cut approach where the generated GMIC are not added to the current LP, but immediately relaxed in a Lagrangian fashion.

title: Cutting plane versus compact formulations for uncertain (integer) linear programs
contribution: A computational comparison of compact robust counterparts and cutting-plane formulations for uncertain LPs and ILPs, with new uncertain set covering and connectivity problems: cuts win for LPs, compact models for ILPs (abstract).

method_links.note: Step 4: the model is chosen per problem class by measurement, but for ILPs the larger compact model beats the projected cutting-plane formulation, so thinning is not the winning move there.

The outcome is that a compact ILP formulation (if available) can be preferable because it allows for a better use of the rich arsenal of preprocessing/cut generation tools available in modern ILP solvers.

assumptions: General MIPs with a given feasible starting solution; wind farm turbine layout as the application (abstract). Venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Sixth RAMP Symposium, Hosei University, Tokyo, October 16-17, 2014, from page 159 (PDF p. 1; works.json had no venue).
proof_devices: proximity objective replacing the original objective inside a black-box MIP solver (abstract)
experiments: Very large scale wind farm instances; practical viability claimed; baselines and metrics not in the abstract (abstract).
positioning: Set against large-neighbourhood search heuristics that restrict constraints (local branching, RINS) (abstract).
limits_future: Effective 'at least when the landscape of feasible solutions is not too irregular' (abstract).

method_links.note: The black-box MIP solver is the heuristic's engine; the method changes only what it is asked to optimize (the objective), not the solver.

transferable: To improve an incumbent with a black-box MIP solver, change the objective (a proximity function) instead of adding neighbourhood constraints, and state the landscape condition under which this pays (abstract).
coauthors: Martina Fischetti (first author; Aalborg University per p. 1), M. Monaci

quotes.text: Proximity search is an alternative approach, still aimed at improving a given feasible solution: instead of modifying the constraints of the MIP at hand with the aim of reducing search space, one modifies the objective function to make the search easier.
The approach can be quite effective in quickly improving a given starting feasible solution, at least when the landscape of feasible solutions is not too irregular.

title: Optimal turbine allocation for offshore and onshore wind farms
contribution: A MILP-based heuristic for turbine positioning in offshore and onshore wind farms, viable on very large instances (abstract).
problem_entry: Wind farm design, where an efficient use of resources decides economic success; turbine positioning as one of the most relevant design problems (abstract).
key_idea: A heuristic based on MILP techniques; which one is not said in the abstract (abstract). S154 (RAMP 2014) applies proximity search to turbine layout, possibly the same heuristic, not checked (inferred).
assumptions: Turbine positioning for offshore and onshore wind farms (abstract).
experiments: Very large scale instances; practical viability claimed; details not in the abstract (abstract).

quotes.text: In the present paper we address the optimization of turbine positions, which is one of the most relevant problems in the design of a wind farm, and propose a heuristic approach based on Mixed-Integer Linear Programming techniques.

title: Intersection Cuts for Bilevel Optimization
contribution: A general-purpose exact MIBLP solver built from minimal additions to a MILP branch-and-cut code (IPCO version of the intersection-cut bilevel work) (abstract).
problem_entry: The exact solution of bilevel optimization problems as a very challenging task with a flourishing recent literature (abstract).
key_idea: Solve generic MIBLPs to proven optimality by a general-purpose approach applicable to any MIBLP under mild conditions, built from the minimal additions that turn an effective MILP branch-and-cut code into a valid MIBLP solver and so inherit its cuts, branching rules and heuristics (abstract). The intersection cuts of the title are not described in the abstract on file (inferred from title).
assumptions: MIBLPs with all constraints linear and some or all variables integer, 'under mild conditions' (abstract).
proof_devices: minimal additions converting a MILP branch-and-cut code into a valid MIBLP solver (abstract)
experiments: Not described in the abstract on file (abstract).
positioning: General-purpose rather than ad-hoc methods for specific cases (abstract).

method_links.note: Steps 1 and 3: only minimal additions to a MILP branch-and-cut code, which keeps its cuts, branching rules and heuristics; IPCO 2016 version of the S027 card's evidence.

transferable: Build a solver for a harder class as the minimal set of additions to a stock MILP branch-and-cut code, so that it keeps the code's cuts, branching rules and heuristics (abstract).
coauthors: I. Ljubić, M. Monaci, M. Sinnl

quotes.text: Our approach concentrates on minimal additions required to convert an effective branch-and-cut MILP exact code into a valid MIBLP solver, thus inheriting the wide arsenal of MILP tools (cuts, branching rules, heuristics) available in modern solvers.
In doing so, we look for a general-purpose approach applicable to any MIBLP (under mild conditions), rather than ad-hoc methods for specific cases.

title: Comments on: On learning and branching: a survey
contribution: A two-page discussant's comment on Lodi and Zarpellon's survey on learning and branching; content not read (metadata).
key_idea: Inferred from title (metadata only): a two-page comment (TOP 25(2), pp. 237-238, published 13 June 2017; Crossref) on the invited survey 'On learning and branching: a survey' by A. Lodi and G. Zarpellon (TOP 25(2), pp. 207-236; Crossref, DOI 10.1007/s11750-017-0451-6). The Springer page lists two references: Achterberg's 2007 thesis Constraint integer programming, and Le Bodic and Nemhauser (2017, Mathematical Programming). Padova IRIS records it as a review in a journal ('Recensione in rivista'), with no file. No abstract: none on the Springer page, in Crossref or in OpenAlex (metadata).

title: Matheuristics
contribution: A handbook chapter introducing matheuristics, heuristics built around a mathematical programming model, through wind farm, packing and vehicle routing examples (abstract).
problem_entry: Defines a matheuristic as the hybridization of mathematical programming with metaheuristics, whose hallmark is the central role of the model around which the heuristic is built (abstract).
key_idea: Matheuristics as a concept framework for mathematically sound heuristics, not a rigid paradigm; main ideas introduced through wind farm, packing and vehicle routing applications (abstract).
positioning: Tutorial chapter (Chapter 5 of the Handbook of Heuristics per DTU Orbit, keywords Heuristics, Large scale neighborhood search, Local branching, Mathematical programming, Matheuristics) (metadata). Updated in 2025 as S051, with an almost identical abstract (abstract).
writing: Teaches by three worked applications rather than by a taxonomy (abstract).

method_links.note: Stated, joint (with Martina Fischetti): the mathematical programming model sits at the centre and the heuristic is built around it; the abstract does not say that a general-purpose solver does the work.

quotes.text: The hallmark of matheuristics is the central role played by the mathematical programming model, around which the overall heuristic is built.
As such, matheuristic is not a rigid paradigm but rather a concept framework for the design of mathematically sound heuristics.

title: Introduction to mathematical optimization
contribution: An introductory textbook on LP, ILP, complexity and graph theory with emphasis on branch-and-cut (abstract).
problem_entry: A teaching aid for students of Operations Research and Mathematical Optimization courses in scientific faculties (abstract; book description, source Amazon per abstract-sources.json).
key_idea: Linear programming, integer linear programming, computational complexity and graph theory, with particular emphasis on ILP and recent resolution techniques, in particular branch-and-cut; many examples and exercises (abstract).
positioning: Homepage lists it as a Kindle e-book in English, next to the Italian Lezioni di Ricerca Operativa (metadata).

quotes.text: Particular emphasis is given to Integer Linear Programming, with an exposition of the most recent resolution techniques, and in particular of the branch-and-cut method.

title: Integrated layout and cable routing in wind farm optimal design
contribution: An integrated turbine-layout and cable-routing MILP strengthened by combinatorially valid Benders-like clique cuts, inside an exact branch-and-cut whose success depends on them (abstract).
problem_entry: Combined optimization of turbine locations and of the connection cables to a substation, and eventually to shore, in offshore wind farm design (abstract).
key_idea: A MILP combining earlier proposals, strengthened by inequalities including new Benders-like cuts from an induced-clique substructure, proved valid combinatorially without Benders duality and separated efficiently, inside an exact branch-and-cut (abstract).
assumptions: Offshore wind farm: turbine location plus cable routing to a substation (abstract).
proof_devices: new classes of Benders-like cuts from an induced-clique substructure (abstract)
combinatorial validity proof without Benders's standard duality theory (abstract)
efficient separation of the new cuts at run time in an exact branch-and-cut (abstract)
experiments: Computational tests: the cuts very significantly improve the standard model's dual bound and are instrumental for the exact solver; data released as supplemental material at the article DOI (abstract).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Benders-like cuts derived from an induced-clique substructure of the problem.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: release solver, instances and optimal values (existing)
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Data only: 'Data are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.4470' (supplemental material).

transferable: Derive Benders-like cuts from a small substructure (induced cliques) and prove their validity combinatorially, without LP duality, then separate them at run time in an exact branch-and-cut (abstract).

quotes.text: In particular, we propose new classes of Benders-like cuts derived from an induced-clique substructure of the problem.
The validity of these cuts is established in a purely combinatorial way, without resorting to Benders’s standard duality theory, and efficient separation procedures are proposed.

title: Matheuristics by Examples
contribution: The 2025 update of the matheuristics handbook chapter, with the same three examples and an almost identical abstract (abstract).
problem_entry: Same definition as D016: matheuristics hybridize mathematical programming with metaheuristics, the model at the centre (abstract).
key_idea: The main matheuristic ideas illustrated by the same three applications (wind farm, packing, vehicle routing) (abstract).
positioning: The abstract is D016's word for word except 'in the fields of' for 'in the field of', so the entry is presumably an update of the 2018 chapter under a new title (abstract compared with D016's; inferred). Editors Martí, Pardalos and Resende (homepage list); Padova IRIS (hdl 11577/3545751) holds the publisher's PDF under restricted access, not downloaded (metadata).

method_links.note: Stated, joint (with Martina Fischetti): as in D016, the model sits at the centre of the heuristic; the abstract does not say that a general-purpose solver does the work.

quotes.text: The aim of this chapter is to introduce the main matheuristic ideas.
Three specific applications in the fields of wind farm, packing, and vehicle routing optimization, respectively, are addressed and used to illustrate the main features of the method.

title: Column Generation Algorithms for the Pickup and Delivery Problem with Time Windows and Last-in-First-out Loading
contribution: A column-generation bounding procedure for the PDPTW with LIFO loading over non-necessarily elementary routes, giving tight bounds in seconds on benchmark instances (abstract).
problem_entry: The PDPTWL: serve pickup and delivery locations within time windows at minimum cost with capacitated vehicles under a Last-in-First-out loading policy (abstract).
key_idea: Column generation solving the LP relaxation of a set partitioning formulation whose variables are non-necessarily elementary routes (abstract).
assumptions: Pickup and delivery with time windows, capacitated vehicles, LIFO loading; set partitioning over non-necessarily elementary routes (abstract).
proof_devices: column generation for the LP relaxation of a set partitioning formulation over non-necessarily elementary routes (abstract)
experiments: Benchmark instances from the literature; tight dual bounds computed in a few seconds; no exact method yet (abstract).
limits_future: The bounding procedure 'can be a building block of an exact method for the PDPTWL', the stated next step (abstract). Padova IRIS (hdl 11577/3555881) holds the publisher's PDF under restricted access (metadata).

quotes.text: We propose a bounding procedure based on column generation to find tight dual bounds to the PDPTWL by solving the linear relaxation of a set partitioning formulation, where variables correspond to (non-necessarily elementary) routes.
Therefore, the bounding procedure can be a building block of an exact method for the PDPTWL.
